title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover ordering under high load
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: During a regional outage test we observed a window where multiple concurrent failover attempts and SLO-enforcer backoff updates caused out-of-order region promotions. This could briefly send traffic to a node pool that was still ramping, causing elevated tail latency and cascading circuit-breaker tripping. Impact: intermittent increased error-rate and high p99 latency in Hosted during synthetic high-QPS experiments and a customer-facing incident (SUP-501). Root cause: a race between the regional failover coordinator and the SLO enforcer's backoff/hysteresis update path. Under high concurrency the coordinator could enqueue multiple failover attempts which raced with backoff smoothing updates, resulting in ordering inversions and duplicate promotions. Fix summary: 1) Introduce an epoch token for regional failover operations to enforce monotonic ordering and make concurrent attempts idempotent. 2) Serialize critical path updates in the enforcer using a light-weight compare-and-swap (CAS) on the region epoch rather than coarse global locks. 3) Add de-duplication and a short randomized jitter on retry to prevent thundering herd on promotion. 4) Tighten hysteresis thresholds and introduce a configurable smoothing window to avoid oscillation during partial capacity recoveries. 5) Add targeted unit and e2e tests that simulate concurrent failover/backoff races and a small integration test that runs a scaled synthetic workload in the perf-canary environment. Operational rollout: hotfix gated to staging, perf-canary, then gradual rollout to Hosted and Dedicated over 30 minutes with automatic rollback on SLO regression. Monitoring: new metrics added (slo_enforcer.failover_epoch, slo_enforcer.concurrent_failover_attempts, slo_enforcer.promotion_duplicates) and an alert that fires if duplicated promotions > 5 in 1m. Backport: backported core safety fixes to the 2025.12 release branch for affected Dedicated customers. Notes: this is a targeted stability hotfix; no model or API behavior changed. The PR description includes the reproduction steps and test harness used for verification.

review_comments: Marco Alvarez: Please add a high-level comment on why epoch tokens are safe across process restarts - are they persisted or reconstructed?
Aisha Patel: Epochs are reconstructed from the region generation ID stored in the cluster state; added explanation + inline comment in coordination.rs
Lin Zhou: The CAS looks good, but consider a metrics counter to surface dropped duplicate attempts - added metric and tests in the latest commit.
Priya Menon: Can we ensure the randomized jitter bound is configurable via a feature flag? I prefer it adjustable for Dedicated customers. - added config flag with default 50-200ms and note in docs.
Lin Zhou: Integration test flaked in CI on first run (race in perf-canary harness) - reran and passed after adding a small stabilization sleep in harness.
Marco Alvarez: Approving after addressing comments and CI green.
merge_info: merged via squash-and-merge by Marco Alvarez (merge commit 3a4f2b). Post-merge: staged rollout to perf-canary at 2026-02-22T14:10Z, gradual 30m rollout to Hosted and Dedicated. No rollback needed.
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize regional failover ordering in SLO enforcer to prevent transient promotions and p99 latency spikes. Added metrics and alerting for duplicate promotions. Backported to 2025.12.
notes_for_on_call: If you see repeated slo_enforcer.promotion_duplicates > 5/min, trigger rollback to previous release and contact the slo-enforcer oncall. Monitor slo_enforcer.failover_epoch drift and the perf-canary dashboards during rollout.
testing_and_verification: Unit + concurrency tests added and run locally. Integration run in perf-canary using synthetic load (slo-enforcer-race.py) to reproduce previous failure mode. Verified no SLO regressions and p99 improvement in canary compared to baseline.
changelog_entry: Hotfix: SLO enforcer regional failover ordering stabilization (ENG-3421).
additional_context: Related: ENG-3490 investigated larger failover rearchitecture; this hotfix is minimal and safe to land quickly to mitigate customer impact while larger changes are planned.
